record.paper_title: Open Questions in the Understanding of Strangeness Production in HIC – Experiment Perspective
record.original_question: At intermediate heavy-ion collision energies, especially SPS energies and below, how much of the observed strangeness enhancement can be generated by hadronic-medium mechanisms such as multi-step hadronic reactions, resonances, or multi-meson fusion processes rather than by partonic matter?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In relativistic heavy-ion collisions at intermediate center-of-mass energies (those of the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron and below, i.e. roughly √s_NN ≲ 17 GeV), an enhancement of strange-hadron yields per participating nucleon is observed in nucleus–nucleus collisions relative to elementary proton–proton reactions, with the enhancement being most pronounced for multi-strange baryons. Such an enhancement has historically been interpreted as a signature of a deconfined partonic phase (quark–gluon plasma). However, a dense hadronic medium can also generate additional strangeness through purely hadronic mechanisms, including: (i) multi-step inelastic hadronic reactions producing strange–antistrange pairs, (ii) excitation, propagation, and decay of baryonic and mesonic resonances carrying strangeness, and (iii) multi-meson fusion processes of the schematic form n_1 π + n_2 K + … → Y (with Y a strange or multi-strange (anti-)baryon), which respect strangeness conservation while bypassing high thresholds of binary reactions.

Problem. Provide a quantitative determination of the maximum fraction of the observed strangeness enhancement at SPS energies and below that can be accounted for by hadronic-medium mechanisms alone (multi-step hadronic reactions, resonance dynamics, and multi-meson fusion), as opposed to mechanisms requiring partonic degrees of freedom. Concretely, for each strange species s ∈ {K, Λ, Ξ, Ω, and their antiparticles} and each √s_NN in the SPS range, compute within a consistent hadronic transport framework that includes all of (i)–(iii) the predicted enhancement factor E_s^had(√s_NN), and compare it with the experimentally measured enhancement E_s^exp(√s_NN), thereby establishing whether E_s^had can saturate E_s^exp or whether a residual partonic contribution is required.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature indicates the question remains open. While multi-meson fusion in hadronic transport models has been shown to reduce the gap between hadronic predictions and measured (multi-)strange anti-baryon yields, a systematic and quantitative evaluation across SPS energies has not yet been completed, largely due to computational cost. Recent NA61/SHINE results (2025) and ongoing transport-model studies continue to investigate the issue without a definitive resolution.

status_evidence.title: News on strangeness production from the NA61/SHINE experiment (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent NA61/SHINE results at SPS energies continue to probe strangeness production mechanisms in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions.
status_evidence.claim: The experimental program at SPS energies investigating hadronic vs. partonic origin of strangeness enhancement is still ongoing as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: Strange hadron production in heavy ion collisions from SPS to RHIC (1105.2798)
status_evidence.snippet: Multi-meson fusion processes can contribute to strange anti-baryon yields in a dense hadronic medium and may reduce the discrepancy between hadronic models and data; a systematic quantitative evaluation has not been performed.
status_evidence.claim: The quantitative contribution of hadronic mechanisms (including multi-meson fusion) to strangeness enhancement at SPS energies remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Exploring strangeness enhancement with EPOS4 (Phys. Rev. D)
status_evidence.snippet: Modern event generators continue to refine descriptions of strangeness enhancement, indicating no consensus closed answer.
status_evidence.claim: Strangeness enhancement modeling remains an active research topic.
